Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the RetailWave Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to RetailWave's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Thompson, CEO; Mike Chen, CFO; Lisa Patel, COO; Jordan Lee, CMO; Raj Singh, CTO; and Elena Vasquez, CDO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, CEO of RetailWave.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by effective seasonality management and accelerated revenue growth. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV and active buyers.

Our focus remains on boosting order frequency through evolving customer habits. We are also excited about the progress in our international market expansion, which delivered impressive performance metrics.

We are investing heavily in advertising and marketing spend efficiency, particularly improving our return on ad spend. Mobile app engagement has shown strong gains in downloads, active users, and conversion rates.

Finally, we are committed to optimizing the impact of promotional activities on both sales velocity and profitability.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Chen, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Our Q2 revenue was $25.6 billion, an increase of 18% year-over-year. Gross margin was 35.2%, driven by higher take rates, optimized private-label assortments, and supply chain efficiencies. Operating expenses were $8.5 billion, representing 33% of revenue. Our marketing investments yielded strong returns, with ROAS climbing across channels.

Our net income for the quarter was $1.8 billion, or $1.25 per share. We ended the quarter with $12.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of $105 to $110 billion in revenue.

As we dive deeper into our Q2 results, I'd like to spend some time on seasonality—a defining characteristic of our business here at RetailWave, where we operate a leading multi-category e-commerce marketplace with over 150 million active users globally. E-commerce seasonality stems from predictable consumer cycles: holiday peaks in Q4, back-to-school ramps in Q3, and softer periods in Q1 and Q2, accented by events like Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, and our own Prime Day-style events. Our Gross Merchandise Value—or GMV—typically shows a 3:1 ratio between peak Q4 and trough Q1 quarters, with Q4 historically making up 35-40% of annual GMV.

Over the past five years, we've observed robust seasonality boosted by digital adoption. In FY2020, during COVID lockdowns, Q4 GMV jumped 55% year-over-year to $28 billion, powered by a 120% traffic surge and a 15% lift in Average Order Value from impulse buys in home & garden and electronics categories, such as fitness gear and smart doorbells. By FY2022, post-recovery normalization tempered Q4 GMV growth to 32% year-over-year at $42 billion as shoppers returned to physical stores. In FY2023, Q4 reached $48 billion, up 14% year-over-year, with conversion rates rising to 4.2% due to our AI-driven recommendation engine, which increased cross-sell rates by 22%.

This year, first-half GMV totaled $52 billion, up 12% year-over-year. Q1 GMV was $18.5 billion, flat year-over-year but beating our internal forecast by 2%—stronger than the anticipated 5% dip, thanks to steady demand in essentials like groceries and beauty. Q2 accelerated to $33.5 billion, up 18% year-over-year and exceeding guidance by 4 points. Traffic rose 14% to 2.8 billion sessions, AOV increased 3% to $85, and active buyers grew 9% to 45 million. This compares favorably to our five-year Q2 average of 22% growth, though below pandemic peaks amid normalization.

Regarding deviations—and their implications for guidance—Q2 seasonality beat our model by 300 basis points, mainly from an early Easter boosting apparel and gifting by 25% in North America, plus APAC surges from Ramadan promotions where fashion GMV rose 35% year-over-year. However, Q1 saw a 5% miss in winter categories like outerwear and heating appliances, dropping to $2.1 billion from $2.2 billion last year, due to the mildest U.S. winter in decades with temperatures 4°F above average, cutting demand for jackets and heaters by 18%. In Europe, lingering Brexit effects and new DSA regulations slowed cross-border fulfillment, limiting Q1 GMV growth to 8% versus 15% expected.

Regionally, North America (55% of GMV) followed textbook patterns in Q2: Mother's Day lifted AOV 28% to $112, with beauty and jewelry up 42%, akin to early Prime Day previews. Inflation led some trading down, with mid-tier electronics showing 12% unit growth but flat dollars as AOV fell 2%. APAC (25% of GMV) overdelivered with 22% Q2 growth; India's IPL season and China's 618 analogs pushed electronics GMV to $8.2 billion, up 30%, via partnerships with local players. Europe (15%) grew 7% amid energy crises hurting home goods by 9%, but UEFA Euros tie-ins set up Q3. LATAM (5%) surged 25% from Carnival momentum, with soccer gear booming.

We've countered seasonality risks with tech: our ML demand forecasting model on Snowflake and TensorFlow hits 92% SKU-level accuracy, up from 85%, enabling 20% more pre-positioned inventory in hubs like Louisville. Dynamic pricing on 15 million SKUs captured 8% margin uplift. Omnichannel via RetailWave Connect API boosted BOPIS 40%. Blockchain vendor tracking cut stockouts to 4% from 12%, scaling private-label like Wave Essentials to $4 billion run-rate.

Strategically, we're diversifying from holidays: health & wellness now 18% of GMV, up from 12%, with 15% steady growth via subscriptions yielding 3x LTV. CAC stayed at $28 despite 14% traffic growth, via cheaper TikTok integrations. Wave Rewards lifted repeats 22%, VIPs spending 4.5x more. Inventory turns hit 8.2x, safety stock at 14 weeks for Q4.

Ahead, Q3 back-to-school eyes $28 billion GMV, up 25%, with early promos showing 15% pre-order lift. Q4 guidance $55-58 billion, +15-20%. Risks like port strikes are mitigated by 30% more air freight capacity. Overall, seasonality is a tailwind, with management via tech and balance driving 16% full-year GMV growth and 200 bps take-rate expansion to 19.5%.

Turning to revenue growth specifically, which was a standout this quarter, underscoring our marketplace strength amid e-commerce dynamics. We guided $24.5-25.0 billion, implying 13-15% year-over-year growth; we delivered $25.6 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 2% above midpoint, with 8% quarter-over-quarter from Q1's $23.7 billion on seasonal momentum and share gains.

Revenue broke down as marketplace fees (52%, $13.3 billion, +22%), on 25% GMV growth to $85 billion and take rates to 15.7% via NovaPro tools; direct retail (28%, $7.2 billion, +12%) with private-label gains; advertising (14%, $3.6 billion, +28%) via GenAI placements; subscriptions (6%, $1.5 billion, +15%) from 185 million NovaPrime members.

Year-over-year 18% beat industry ~10%, with 14% active customers to 420 million, 5% AOV to $72 on 35% better AI conversions, 68% repeats. QoQ 8% topped 6-7% guide on 10% GMV ramp, 72% mobile orders.

North America (65%, $16.6 billion, +16%) gained share via NovaLocal delivery in 85% MSAs. APAC (22%, $5.6 billion, +27%) exploded in SEA/India. EMEA (10%, $2.6 billion, +11%) held via personalization.

Our Flywheel 2.0 boosts delivery to 95%, NPS to 78, cloud pricing cuts churn. This sets up H2 for 15%+ growth.

Next, order frequency, a key LTV indicator—average orders per active customer over 12 months. Q2 saw 14% year-over-year rise to 2.3, beating 10% target, trailing 12-month at 2.1 from 1.8. Tops industry 8-10%, with subscribers (28% base) at 4.7x non-subs.

Drivers: post-stockpile shift to replenishment—AOV down 2% QoQ to $48, but frequency up 7% in consumables; AI SmartCart with 92% opens, one-click reorders, 22% lift in app users (65% orders).

North America +16% to 2.5 on same-day; APAC +25% to 2.0 on micro-orders; EMEA +5% to 1.9 post-regs.

Investing $150 million in Frequency Rewards, cross-nudges. Guide 12-15% full-year.

On international expansion, now 28% GMV up from 22%, $1.2 billion revenue +52%. GMV $4.8 billion +58%, MAUs 145 million +42%, take rates 18.5%, LTV/CAC 3.8x, margins 14.2%.

Europe (42%, $2.0B +32%): UK share 8.2%, Germany/France strong on BNPL. SEA/India (38%, $1.8B +92%): India $900M +115%, SEA languages/partners. LATAM (15%, $720M +45%): Brazil PIX.

Tech: AWS edge, AI pricing, blockchain supply, 150 payments. Guide 50-55% FY24 GMV growth.

For advertising efficiency, ROAS hit 7.2x +18%, aiding 25 bps EBITDA expansion. Spend $185 million +12%, CAC $42 -9%.

Paid search 9.1x on ML bidding; social 6.4x TikTok influencers; RMNs 8.7x Amazon/Walmart; owned 12.5x.

North America 7.8x, EMEA 6.5x, APAC 6.9x. MTA models, AI personalization lift CTR 28%.

Target 8x+ year-end.

Mobile app: 4.2M downloads +32%, MAUs 28.5M +25%, DAUs 9.2M, retention D1 52%. CVR 4.8% +22%, iOS 5.9%.

GenAI recs, Flutter, SSA. 65% orders app. Guide Q3 4.8-5.2M downloads.

Finally, promotions drove 28% GMV to $18.2B, +35% volume, AOV +12% $85, CVR to 5.1%. NA back-to-school +42%, APAC +55%.

Margins down 180 bps to 32.4%, but EBITDA steady on fulfillment -8%. New cohorts 2.5x LTV. Promo Intelligence optimizes.

Guide Q3 22-25% GMV, margins +100 bps.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa to discuss operations.

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, Mike. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and fulfillment optimization. Our shipping times improved by 25%. Fulfillment costs dropped 12%. We are implementing advanced robotics in our mega-centers.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan.

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Lisa. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from targeted social campaigns and RMN partnerships. Customer acquisition costs were $28, down from last year. Our brand awareness increased by 20%. We are focusing on personalized retention marketing.

Now I'll turn it over to Raj.

Raj Singh:
Thanks, Jordan. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization and cloud infrastructure upgrades. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 25%. We're investing in edge computing and GenAI.

Now I'll turn it over to Elena.

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Raj. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 20% improvement in conversion rates because of advanced ML models. We are also focusing on privacy-enhancing technologies.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Sarah, could you expand on the seasonality deviations, particularly in Q1 winter categories and how you're adjusting forecasts?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, John. Absolutely, the mild U.S. winter hit outerwear and appliances hard, down 18% as temperatures were 4°F above average. But Q2's early Easter and APAC Ramadan more than offset, beating models by 300 bps. Our ML forecasting at 92% accuracy and inventory pre-positioning have us well-set for Q3 and Q4, with $28B and $55-58B GMV guided.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. Mike, on revenue growth, how sustainable is the 18% YoY with tough comps, and regional breakdowns?

Mike Chen:
Emily, thanks. The 18% was broad-based—marketplace +22%, ads +28%—beating industry 10%. NA +16% on delivery networks, APAC +27% partnerships. Flywheel improvements like 95% OTD sustain it into H2 for 15%+ full-year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
Thanks. Lisa, regarding order frequency at 2.3, what drove the APAC surge, and risks to guidance?

Lisa Patel:
Good question, David. APAC's 25% jump to 2.0 came from hyperlocal quick-commerce in India/Indonesia, micro-orders despite low AOV. SmartCart AI and rewards tiers support 12-15% full-year guide; macro softening is a watch but retention moat strong.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays.

Rachel Kim:
Congrats. Jordan, on international promo impacts—how did they affect ROAS and profitability?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Rachel. Promos accelerated GMV 28% but compressed margins 180 bps; retention ROAS at 6.8x offset acquisition dips to 3.1x. Regional tailoring—like Diwali cashback—lifted APAC CVR to 7.2%, with LTV 2.5x for promo cohorts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Citi.

Tom Rivera:
Thanks. Raj, mobile app CVR up 22% to 4.8%—tech details and iOS vs Android?

Raj Singh:
Tom, key was SwiftMatch GenAI recs +18% CVR, Flutter for parity, SSA for privacy. iOS 5.9% vs Android 3.9%, but EM volume balances. App now 65% orders, guiding 5.0-5.3% Q4.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Patel with Deutsche Bank.

Anna Patel:
Solid quarter. Elena, advertising efficiency—channel shifts and cookieless future?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Anna. ROAS 7.2x: search 9.1x, social 6.4x, RMNs 8.7x. MTA and AI shifted 12% budget; 70% server-side targeting hedges cookies. Target 8x+ via data moats.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
